title: Nuancer un argumentaire / Nuancing an argument
bridge: In Spanish, we often qualify arguments with connectors like 'sin embargo' (however), 'no obstante' (nevertheless), or 'aunque' (even though), and the subjunctive helps us express concession. In French, concession and opposition are constructed with more varied and often more formal structures, such as 'encore que' (even though), 'si tant est que' (if indeed), or the use of the subjunctive after 'bien que' (although) and 'quoique' (even though). A common trap is using 'malgré que' (despite that) with the indicative, when standard French requires the subjunctive (or prefers 'malgré + noun'). Additionally, French distinguishes between 'cependant' (however) and 'pourtant' (yet, with a nuance of contradiction), whereas Spanish tends to use a single connector.
rule: To qualify an argument in French at C1 level, different mechanisms are used: 1) Opposition and concession connectors: 'cependant', 'pourtant', 'néanmoins', 'toutefois' (however), which are followed by an independent clause. 2) Concessive phrases requiring the subjunctive: 'bien que', 'quoique', 'encore que' (even though), followed by the subjunctive. 3) Structures with 'avoir beau + infinitive' (no matter how much), which express a useless concession. 4) 'Si + indicative' with concessive value (if it is true that). 5) 'Même si' (even if) takes the indicative, unlike 'bien que'. 6) To qualify an assertion, adverbs like 'certes' (certainly), 'assurément' (undoubtedly), 'sans doute' (no doubt), 'peut-être' (perhaps) are used. 7) The conditional is key to softening statements: 'je dirais que' (I would say that), 'il faudrait' (it would be necessary), etc. Be careful: 'malgré que' is criticized by standard usage; it is better to use 'bien que' or 'quoique' followed by the subjunctive, or reformulate with 'malgré + noun' (malgré ma fatigue) or 'malgré le fait que + subjunctive' (even though, legally acceptable but less elegant). In formal register, 'encore que' is used to restrict what is said, with the subjunctive.

concept_examples.text: Certes, le projet est ambitieux, mais il reste réalisable.
concept_examples.translation: Ciertamente, el proyecto es ambicioso, pero sigue siendo realizable.
concept_examples.phonetic: /sɛʁtə lə pʁɔʒɛ ɛt‿ɑ̃bisjø mɛ il ʁɛst ʁəalizabl/

concept_examples.text: Bien que les résultats soient encourageants, il faut rester prudent.
concept_examples.translation: Aunque los resultados sean alentadores, hay que ser prudente.
concept_examples.phonetic: /bjɛ̃ kə le ʁezylta swaʁ‿ɑ̃kuʁaʒɑ̃ il fo ʁɛste pʁydɑ̃/

concept_examples.text: Il a beau insister, je ne changerai pas d'avis.
concept_examples.translation: Por más que insista, no cambiaré de opinión.
concept_examples.phonetic: /il a bo ɛ̃siste ʒə nə ʃɑ̃ʒəʁe pa davis/

concept_examples.text: Je dirais que cette solution est envisageable, à condition que les coûts soient maîtrisés.
concept_examples.translation: Yo diría que esta solución es viable, siempre que los costos estén controlados.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒə diʁɛ kə sɛt sɔlysjɔ̃ ɛt‿ɑ̃vizaʒabl a kɔ̃disjɔ̃ kə le ku swaʁ mɛtʁize/

common_error.wrong: Malgré que je sois fatigué, je continue.
common_error.correct: Bien que je sois fatigué, je continue.
common_error.explanation: The error comes from a direct translation of the Spanish 'aunque' using 'malgré que'. In standard French, 'malgré que' is considered incorrect or highly criticized; it is better to use 'bien que' or 'quoique' followed by the subjunctive, or reformulate with 'malgré + noun' (malgré ma fatigue) or 'malgré le fait que + subjunctive' (even though, legally acceptable but less elegant).

examples.original: Le projet est ambitieux; pourtant, il demeure réalisable.
examples.phonetic: /lə pʁɔʒɛ ɛt‿ɑ̃bisjø puʁtɑ̃ il dəmœʁ ʁealizabl/
examples.translation: El proyecto es ambicioso; sin embargo, sigue siendo realizable.
examples.note: 'Pourtant' indicates a stronger contradiction than 'cependant'.

examples.original: Cette politique a des avantages; néanmoins, elle présente des risques.
examples.phonetic: /sɛt pɔlitik a de avɑ̃taʒ neɑ̃mwɛ̃ ɛl pʁezɑ̃t de ʁisk/
examples.translation: Esta política tiene ventajas; no obstante, presenta riesgos.
examples.note: 'Néanmoins' is more formal than 'cependant' and is used in formal register.

examples.original: Le raisonnement est logique; toutefois, certaines données manquent.
examples.phonetic: /lə ʁɛzɔnmɑ̃ ɛ lɔʒik tutfwa sɛʁtɛn dɔne mɑ̃k/
examples.translation: El razonamiento es lógico; sin embargo, faltan ciertos datos.
examples.note: 'Toutefois' introduces a specific restriction.

examples.original: Quoiqu'il soit compétent, il manque d'expérience.
examples.phonetic: /kwak‿il swa kɔ̃petɑ̃ il mɑ̃k dɛkspeʁjɑ̃s/
examples.translation: Aunque sea competente, le falta experiencia.
examples.note: 'Quoique' is written as one word and requires the subjunctive; be careful not to confuse it with 'quoi que' (whatever).

examples.original: Encore que les chiffres soient discutables, la tendance est claire.
examples.phonetic: /ɑ̃kɔʁ kə le ʃifʁ swaʁ diskytabl la tɑ̃dɑ̃s ɛ klɛʁ/
examples.translation: Aunque las cifras sean discutibles, la tendencia es clara.
examples.note: 'Encore que' is used to soften an objection and is very formal.

examples.original: Si l'argument est séduisant, il n'emporte pas la conviction.
examples.phonetic: /si laʁgymɑ̃ ɛ sedɥizɑ̃ il nɑ̃pɔʁt pa la kɔ̃viksjɔ̃/
examples.translation: Si bien el argumento es atractivo, no convence.
examples.note: 'Si' with concessive value is used with the indicative.

examples.original: Je serais plutôt enclin à accepter cette offre, à condition de renégocier le prix.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə səʁɛ plytɔ ɑ̃klɛ̃ a aksɛpte sɛt ɔfʁ a kɔ̃disjɔ̃ də ʁənegosje lə pʁi/
examples.translation: Yo estaría más bien inclinado a aceptar esta oferta, siempre que se renegocie el precio.
examples.note: The conditional allows for a softened and polite expression of opinion.

examples.original: Ce point de vue est sans doute pertinent, mais il faudrait le nuancer.
examples.phonetic: /sə pwɛ̃ də vy ɛ sɑ̃ dut pɛʁtinɑ̃ mɛ il fodʁɛ lə nɥɑ̃se/
examples.translation: Este punto de vista es sin duda pertinente, pero habría que matizarlo.
examples.note: 'Sans doute' without negation expresses probability; with negation ('sans aucun doute') it expresses certainty.

examples.original: L'approche est peut-être trop radicale; il conviendrait de l'assouplir.
examples.phonetic: /lapʁɔʃ ɛ pøt‿ɛtʁ tʁo ʁadikal il kɔ̃vjɛ̃dʁɛ də lasuplik/
examples.translation: El enfoque quizás sea demasiado radical; convendría suavizarlo.
examples.note: 'Peut-être' can be placed at the beginning or after the verb; in formal register, it is used with inversion.

title: Analyse critique et évaluation d'idées / Critical analysis and evaluation of ideas
bridge: In French, to qualify an opinion or critically evaluate, the subjunctive is used after expressions of doubt or judgment, just like in Spanish, but you need to be careful with constructions like 'il est probable que' (which takes the indicative) versus 'il est possible que' (subjunctive). This contrast often confuses Spanish speakers, since in Spanish both usually take the subjunctive. Additionally, French frequently uses the conditional to soften critical statements ('je dirais que') and impersonal structures like 'il s'avère que' that have no direct equivalent. Pay attention to the use of logical connectors ('néanmoins', 'cependant') which in Spanish are sometimes translated with commas or periods, but in French require stricter syntactic handling.
rule: To express critical analysis and evaluation of ideas in French at C1 level, master the following resources: 1) Subjunctive after verbs and expressions of negative opinion or doubt: 'je ne pense pas que', 'il est douteux que', 'il est peu probable que' (subjunctive), but 'je pense que', 'il est probable que', 'il me semble que' (indicative). 2) Conditional of politeness to soften criticism: 'je dirais que', 'on pourrait considérer que' (followed by indicative). 3) Impersonal evaluation structures: 'il s'avère que', 'il apparaît que' (indicative), 'il est essentiel de noter que'. 4) Logical connectors of concession and opposition: 'bien que' (+ subjunctive), 'encore que' (+ subjunctive), 'cependant', 'néanmoins', 'toutefois' (with inversion or comma). 5) Verbs of judgment with 'de': 'critiquer quelqu'un de faire quelque chose', 'reprocher à quelqu'un de faire quelque chose'. Note: 'douter que' takes the subjunctive, but 'douter de' is followed by a noun or infinitive; 'nier que' in negation takes the subjunctive, in affirmation sometimes the indicative (nuance). Remember that simple negation 'ne' without 'pas' is used in formal registers with certain verbs (je ne saurais dire).

concept_examples.text: Il est essentiel de nuancer cette affirmation, car elle paraît trop catégorique.
concept_examples.translation: It is essential to nuance this statement, as it seems too categorical.
concept_examples.phonetic: /il ɛt‿ɛsɑ̃sjɛl də nyɑ̃se sɛt‿afiʁmasjɔ̃ kaʁ ɛl paʁɛ tʁo kateɡɔʁik/

concept_examples.text: Bien que l'argument soit séduisant, il manque de preuves concrètes.
concept_examples.translation: Although the argument may be seductive, it lacks concrete evidence.
concept_examples.phonetic: /bjɛ̃ kə l‿aʁɡymɑ̃ swa sedɥizɑ̃ il mɑ̃k də pʁøv kɔ̃kʁɛt/

concept_examples.text: Je ne pense pas que cette hypothèse soit vérifiable dans l'état actuel des recherches.
concept_examples.translation: I do not think this hypothesis is verifiable in the current state of research.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒə nə pɑ̃s pa kə sɛt ipɔtɛz swa veʁifjab dɑ̃ l‿eta aktɥɛl de ʁəʃɛʁʃ/

concept_examples.text: On pourrait objecter que cette méthode néglige les aspects culturels.
concept_examples.translation: One might object that this method neglects cultural aspects.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɔ̃ puʁɛ ɔbʒɛkte kə sɛt metɔd neɡliʒ le aspɛ kyltyʁɛl/

common_error.wrong: Je pense pas que c'est une bonne idée, mais je ne suis pas sûr.
common_error.correct: Je ne pense pas que ce soit une bonne idée, mais je ne suis pas sûr.
common_error.correct_alt: Je ne crois pas que ce soit une bonne idée, même si je n'en suis pas certain.
common_error.explanation: The typical error is using the indicative after 'ne pas penser que'. In French, as in Spanish, the negation of an opinion verb requires the subjunctive in the subordinate clause. Spanish speakers often omit the 'ne' in informal registers, but at C1 level it is essential to maintain complete negation. To avoid this, remember: after 'je ne pense pas que', 'je ne crois pas que', 'je ne trouve pas que', always use the subjunctive.

examples.original: Il me semble que cette analyse est partiellement valable, mais elle ignore certains facteurs.
examples.phonetic: /il mə sɑ̃bl kə sɛt analiz ɛ paʁsjɛlman valab mɛ ɛl iɲɔʁ sɛʁtɛ̃ faktœʁ/
examples.translation: It seems to me that this analysis is partially valid, but it ignores certain factors.
examples.note: Use of 'il me semble que' + indicative, equivalent to Spanish 'me parece que' + indicative.

examples.original: Je dirais que l'argument principal manque de solidité, bien qu'il soit intéressant.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə diʁɛ kə l‿aʁɡymɑ̃ pʁɛ̃sipal mɑ̃k də sɔlidite bjɛ̃ k‿il swa ɛ̃teʁesɑ̃/
examples.translation: I would say that the main argument lacks solidity, although it is interesting.
examples.note: The conditional 'je dirais' softens the criticism; 'bien que' requires the subjunctive.

examples.original: À mon avis, cette théorie est séduisante, mais il faut la considérer avec prudence.
examples.phonetic: /a mɔ̃ avi sɛt teɔʁi ɛ sedɥizɑ̃t mɛ il fo la kɔ̃sideʁe avɛk pʁydɑ̃s/
examples.translation: In my opinion, this theory is seductive, but it must be considered with caution.
examples.note: Use of 'il faut' + infinitive for recommendation.

examples.original: On pourrait objecter que cette approche est trop réductrice, car elle néglige la complexité du phénomène.
examples.phonetic: /ɔ̃ puʁɛ ɔbʒɛkte kə sɛt apʁɔʃ ɛ tʁo ʁedyktʁis kaʁ ɛl neɡliʒ la kɔ̃plɛksite dy fenɔmɛn/
examples.translation: One might object that this approach is too reductionist, as it neglects the complexity of the phenomenon.
examples.note: The conditional 'on pourrait' introduces an objection politely; 'car' introduces justification.

examples.original: Il est difficile de souscrire à cette idée, étant donné que les preuves sont insuffisantes.
examples.phonetic: /il ɛ difisil də suskʁiʁ a sɛt ide etɑ̃ dɔne kə le pʁøv sɔ̃ ɛ̃syfizɑ̃t/
examples.translation: It is difficult to subscribe to this idea, given that the evidence is insufficient.
examples.note: The expression 'étant donné que' (given that) introduces an objective cause.

examples.original: Je conteste fermement l'idée que la fin justifie les moyens.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə kɔ̃tɛst fɛʁməmɑ̃ l‿ide kə la fɛ̃ ʒystifi le mwɛ̃/
examples.translation: I firmly contest the idea that the end justifies the means.
examples.note: After 'l'idée que', if the idea is negated, the subjunctive is used; here it is affirmative, so the indicative is used.

examples.original: En définitive, cette proposition présente des avantages indéniables, mais elle comporte aussi des risques considérables.
examples.phonetic: /ɑ̃ definitiv sɛt pʁɔpozisjɔ̃ pʁezɑ̃t de avɑ̃taʒ ɛ̃denjabl mɛ ɛl kɔ̃pɔʁt osi de ʁisk kɔ̃sideʁabl/
examples.translation: In definitive terms, this proposal presents undeniable advantages, but it also entails considerable risks.
examples.note: Use of 'en définitive' to conclude; 'mais' contrasts and 'aussi' adds.

examples.original: Il apparaît que les bénéfices de cette réforme ont été surestimés par ses partisans.
examples.phonetic: /il apaʁɛ kə le benefis də sɛt ʁefɔʁm ɔ̃ ete syʁɛstime paʁ se paʁtizɑ̃/
examples.translation: It appears that the benefits of this reform have been overestimated by its supporters.
examples.note: The impersonal structure 'il apparaît que' + indicative, typical of formal register.

examples.original: En somme, si l'on admet que cette politique a des lacunes, elle n'en demeure pas moins une avancée significative.
examples.phonetic: /ɑ̃ sɔm si l‿ɔ̃ admɛ kə sɛt pɔlitik a de lakyn ɛl n‿ɑ̃ dəmøʁ pa mwɛ̃ yn‿avɑ̃se siɲifikativ/
examples.translation: In short, if we admit that this policy has shortcomings, it nonetheless remains a significant advancement.
examples.note: The phrase 'n'en ... pas moins' expresses concession; attention is required with pronoun order.

translations.en: Critical analysis and evaluation of ideas

title: Ironie, sarcasme et euphémisme / Irony, sarcasm and euphemism
bridge: In Spanish, irony often relies on intonation and markers like 'claro' or 'por supuesto'. In French, in addition to intonation, specific syntactic structures are used, such as negation with 'ne... pas' accompanied by positive adjectives, or the use of the subjunctive to express false concession. A typical error is directly translating the Spanish 'claro' to 'clair', which in French sounds literal and not ironic. To master irony in French, you must learn to invert semantic values: say the opposite of what you think, but with a colloquial register and gestures that indicate it.
rule: Irony in French at C1 level is constructed through several procedures: 1) Litotes: affirming by negating the opposite (e.g., 'Ce n'est pas mauvais' to mean 'it's very good'). 2) Sarcasm with exaggerated intonation and use of hyperbolic adjectives applied to the trivial (e.g., 'C'est génial' said in a traffic jam). 3) Euphemism: replacing harsh terms with softer ones (e.g., 'une personne âgée' instead of 'vieille', 'non voyant' instead of 'aveugle'). 4) False concession with the subjunctive: 'Bien que ce soit...' or 'Soit disant' to express doubt or ridicule. It is crucial to distinguish irony from error: while in Spanish we use 'ya, ya' ironically, in French 'oui, oui' or 'bien sûr' is used with intonation. Additionally, sarcasm in French often inverts formulas of politeness, such as 'Ah, merci !' to mean the opposite. For euphemism, it is important to know politically correct terms and their limits: 'malentendu' instead of 'mentira' in professional contexts, 'disparaître' instead of 'morir' in journalistic language. The key is to use these resources with moderation and according to the formal or informal register.

concept_examples.text: Ah, c'est vraiment génial d'attendre deux heures sous la pluie !
concept_examples.translation: Oh, it's really great to wait two hours in the rain!
concept_examples.phonetic: /a sɛ vʁɛmɑ̃ ʒenjal d‿atɑ̃d døz œʁ su la plɥi/

concept_examples.text: Ce n'est pas mauvais, ce vin.
concept_examples.translation: This wine isn't bad (it's excellent).
concept_examples.phonetic: /sə nɛ pa mɔvɛ sə vɛ̃/

concept_examples.text: Il a un petit problème avec la vérité.
concept_examples.translation: He has a small problem with the truth (he's a liar).
concept_examples.phonetic: /il a œ̃ pəti pʁɔblɛm avɛk la veʁite/

concept_examples.text: Oh, il est très original, ton nouveau copain.
concept_examples.translation: Oh, he's very original, your new boyfriend (he's weird).
concept_examples.phonetic: /o il ɛ tʁɛ oʁiʒinal tɔ̃ nuvo kɔpɛ̃/

common_error.wrong: Clair, tu te moques de moi.
common_error.correct: Bien sûr, tu te moques de moi.
common_error.correct_alt: Évidemment, tu te moques de moi.
common_error.explanation: In Spanish, 'claro' is frequently used as an ironic marker (e.g., 'Claro, ahora me lo dices'). In French, 'clair' does not have this usage; it is an adjective meaning 'clear' in a literal sense. To express irony, 'bien sûr' or 'évidemment' is used with sarcastic intonation. This error stems from direct lexical transfer. To avoid it, it is important to learn typical discourse connectors in spoken French and their associated intonation.

examples.original: C'est le comble de la malchance !
examples.phonetic: /sɛ lə kɔ̃bl də la malʃɑ̃s/
examples.translation: It's the height of bad luck!
examples.note: The phrase 'le comble' is used to highlight an absurd situation, with exaggerated tone.

examples.original: Oh, super, encore une réunion !
examples.phonetic: /o sypeʁ ɑ̃kɔʁ yn ʁeynjɔ̃/
examples.translation: Oh, great, another meeting!
examples.note: The word 'super' with descending and exaggerated intonation expresses the opposite.

examples.original: Vraiment, tu es un génie de la procrastination.
examples.phonetic: /vʁɛmɑ̃ ty ɛ œ̃ ʒeni də la pʁɔkʁastinasjɔ̃/
examples.translation: You're really a genius at procrastination.
examples.note: Applying an exaggerated compliment to a flaw emphasizes irony.

examples.original: Il n'est pas très courageux.
examples.phonetic: /il nɛ pa tʁɛ kuʁaʒø/
examples.translation: He's not very brave (he's a coward).
examples.note: Litotes negates the opposite to affirm something negatively. Here, 'pas très courageux' is an euphemism for coward.

examples.original: Elle nous a quittés.
examples.phonetic: /ɛl nu a kite/
examples.translation: She has left us (she has died).
examples.note: Classic euphemism for death, widely used in formal language.

examples.original: C'est un peu cher, non ?
examples.phonetic: /sɛ ɛ̃ pø ʃɛʁ nɔ̃/
examples.translation: It's a bit expensive, isn't it? (it's very expensive).
examples.note: 'Un peu' with 'non ?' seeking agreement, softens direct criticism.

examples.original: Pourvu qu'il soit à l'heure, pour une fois !
examples.phonetic: /puʁvy k‿il swa a l‿œʁ puʁ yn fwa/
examples.translation: Let's hope he arrives on time, for once!
examples.note: The expression 'pourvu que' + subjunctive expresses an ironic wish, implying it never happens.

examples.original: Bien que ce soit le meilleur, il a perdu.
examples.phonetic: /bjɛ̃ kə swa lə mɛjœʁ il a pɛʁdy/
examples.translation: Even though he's the best, he lost.
examples.note: Concession with 'bien que' followed by a contradiction creates sarcasm.

examples.original: Qu'il fasse beau ou pas, il prend son vélo.
examples.phonetic: /k‿il fas bo u pa il pʁɑ̃ sɔ̃ velo/
examples.translation: Whether it's nice out or not, he takes his bike.
examples.note: The structure 'qu'il fasse...' with subjunctive indicates ridiculous obstinacy and is often sarcastic.

title: Implicatures et actes de langage indirects / Implicatures and indirect speech acts
bridge: In Spanish, politeness is often expressed through the conditional and explicit verb forms ('¿Podrías...?'), while French C1 uses impersonal structures, negation, and the subjunctive to soften statements. A common error is to translate Spanish constructions like 'me preguntaba si...' literally into French as 'je me demandais si...', which sounds too direct in formal contexts. Additionally, French uses the polite imperfect ('je voulais vous demander') and the particle 'donc' to imply without stating, which has no direct equivalent in Spanish.
rule: In French, indirect speech acts rely on conversational implicature: saying something to communicate something else, based on context. For C1 level, master: 1) Attenuating negation: 'Je ne dis pas que...' (I'm not saying that...) to imply disagreement without stating it. 2) Polite conditional: 'Je pourrais vous suggérer...' (I could suggest to you...) to soften a recommendation. 3) Polite imperfect: 'Je voulais vous parler de...' (I wanted to speak to you about...) to tactfully introduce a topic. 4) The concessive use of 'si': 'Si je peux me permettre...' (If I may...). 5) Negative questions: 'Ne devriez-vous pas...?' (Shouldn't you...?) which imply a suggestion. Be careful with the direct translation of '¿por qué no...?' as 'pourquoi ne pas...?' in formal register: in French, 'Ne pourriez-vous pas...?' or 'Et si...?' are preferred.

concept_examples.text: Je ne dis pas que votre idée est mauvaise, mais...
concept_examples.translation: I'm not saying your idea is bad, but...
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒə nə di pa kə vɔtʁ ide ɛ mɔvɛz, mɛ.../

concept_examples.text: Je pourrais vous suggérer de reconsidérer cette option.
concept_examples.translation: I could suggest you reconsider this option.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒə puʁɛ vu sygʒeʁe də ʁəkɔ̃sideʁe sɛt ɔpsjɔ̃/

concept_examples.text: Je voulais vous demander si vous seriez disponible lundi.
concept_examples.translation: I wanted to ask you if you would be available on Monday.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒə vulɛ vu dəmɑ̃de si vu səʁje disponibl lœ̃di/

concept_examples.text: Ne serait-il pas plus simple de procéder autrement ?
concept_examples.translation: Wouldn't it be simpler to proceed differently?
concept_examples.phonetic: /nə səʁe til pa plys sɛ̃pl də pʁɔsede otʁəmɑ̃/

common_error.wrong: Je me demandais si vous pourriez m'aider ?
common_error.correct: Je me demandais si vous pourriez m'aider.
common_error.correct_alt: Je me demandais si vous pourriez m'aider...
common_error.explanation: In French, this construction is a softened statement, not a direct question. Spanish uses interrogative intonation ('¿Me preguntaba si...?'), which in French would be incorrect. You must use a descending tone or ellipsis, or reformulate with 'Je voulais vous demander si...' + inversion. Avoid the question mark to prevent turning the implicature into a literal question.

examples.original: Je ne trouve pas que ce soit une bonne idée.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə nə tʁuv pa kə sə swa yn bɔn ide/
examples.translation: I don't think it's a good idea.
examples.note: Use of the subjunctive after 'ne pas trouver que' to soften criticism.

examples.original: Ce n'est pas que je sois contre, mais...
examples.phonetic: /sə nɛ pa kə ʒə swa kɔ̃tʁ, mɛ.../
examples.translation: It's not that I'm against it, but...
examples.note: Typical structure to introduce an indirect objection.

examples.original: Je ne dis pas ça pour te critiquer, mais...
examples.phonetic: /ʒə nə di pa sa puʁ tə kʁitike, mɛ.../
examples.translation: I'm not saying this to criticize you, but...
examples.note: Implies there is criticism, but it is softened.

examples.original: Tu pourrais peut-être vérifier les chiffres.
examples.phonetic: /ty puʁɛ pøtɛtʁ veʁifje le ʃifʁ/
examples.translation: You could maybe check the figures.
examples.note: Indirect suggestion disguised as a possibility.

examples.original: On pourrait envisager une autre solution.
examples.phonetic: /ɔ̃ puʁɛ ɑ̃vizaʒe yn otʁ sɔlysjɔ̃/
examples.translation: We could consider another solution.
examples.note: The impersonal 'on' + conditional softens the proposal.

examples.original: Je devrais peut-être vous rappeler que...
examples.phonetic: /ʒə dəvʁɛ pøtɛtʁ vu ʁaple kə/
examples.translation: I should maybe remind you that...
examples.note: Implies a warning or criticism in a polite way.

examples.original: C'est malin, ça !
examples.phonetic: /sɛ malɛ̃ sa/
examples.translation: How clever! (ironic)
examples.note: In context, it means the opposite: it's a criticism.

examples.original: Tu es vraiment à l'aise avec les chiffres, toi.
examples.phonetic: /ty ɛ vʁɛmɑ̃ a lɛz avɛk le ʃifʁ twa/
examples.translation: You're really good with numbers, aren't you.
examples.note: Intonation and context reveal the irony.

examples.original: Il fait un temps magnifique pour un pique-nique !
examples.phonetic: /il fɛ œ̃ tɑ̃ maɲifik puʁ œ̃ piknik/
examples.translation: The weather is wonderful for a picnic!
examples.note: Used to imply the opposite if, for example, it's raining.

examples.original: Ah, tu as enfin compris.
examples.phonetic: /a ty a ɑ̃fɛ̃ kɔ̃pʁi/
examples.translation: Ah, you finally understood.
examples.note: In an ironic tone, implies it took a long time.

title: Présentations et discours formels / Formal presentations and speeches
bridge: In Spanish, formal presentations tend to use constructions like 'En primer lugar', 'Por un lado' or 'Me gustaría comenzar'. In formal French, the use of the subjunctive after expressions such as 'bien que' or 'pour que' is mandatory and is often omitted in error. Additionally, connectors like 'd'une part... d'autre part' require syntactic balance that is not always natural in Spanish. Another key difference: the use of the conditional to soften statements is much more common in French than in Spanish, and the pronoun 'on' in formal registers is avoided in favor of 'nous'.
rule: In French, formal presentations and speeches use specific structures: 1) The subjunctive after impersonal expressions of opinion such as 'il est important que', 'il est nécessaire que', 'bien que'. 2) The conditional (present and past) to formulate polite requests and suggestions: 'Je voudrais', 'Il conviendrait de', 'Aurais-je pu...'. 3) Formal connectors: 'd'une part... d'autre part', 'en outre', 'par conséquent', 'en conclusion' that organize the speech. 4) The use of 'nous' instead of 'on' in formal register. 5) Nominalization of verbs: 'la mise en œuvre', 'la prise de décision'. 6) Inverted questions: 'Pourrions-nous...', 'Quels sont les enjeux...'. At C1 level, nuanced mastery is expected, for example, 'il faudrait' is more softened than 'il faut'.

concept_examples.text: Permettez-moi de commencer par vous remercier de votre présence.
concept_examples.translation: Permítanme comenzar agradeciéndoles su presencia.
concept_examples.phonetic: /pɛʁmɛt mwa də kɔmɑ̃se paʁ vu ʁəmɛʁsje də vuʁ pʁezɑ̃s/

concept_examples.text: D'une part, les résultats sont encourageants ; d'autre part, il reste des défis à relever.
concept_examples.translation: Por un lado, los resultados son alentadores; por otro, quedan desafíos por superar.
concept_examples.phonetic: /dyn paʁ le ʁeʒyltɑ̃ sɔ̃t‿ɑ̃kuʁaʒɑ̃ ; dotʁə paʁ, il ʁɛst də defi a ʁəlve/

concept_examples.text: Il est essentiel que nous prenions en compte les enjeux environnementaux.
concept_examples.translation: Es esencial que tengamos en cuenta los desafíos medioambientales.
concept_examples.phonetic: /il ɛt‿esɑ̃sjɛl kə nu pʁənjɔ̃ ɑ̃ kɔ̃t le z‿ɑ̃ʒø ɑ̃viʁɔnmɑ̃to/

concept_examples.text: Pour conclure, je souhaiterais souligner l'importance de notre collaboration.
concept_examples.translation: Para concluir, quisiera subrayar la importancia de nuestra colaboración.
concept_examples.phonetic: /puʁ kɔ̃klyʁ, ʒə swɛtəʁe suliɲe l‿ɛ̃pɔʁtɑ̃s də nɔtʁ kɔ̃labɔʁasjɔ̃/

common_error.wrong: 2+2=5, c'est une erreur que je voudrais signaler.
common_error.correct: Deux plus deux font cinq, c'est une erreur que je voudrais signaler.
common_error.correct_alt: Deux plus deux égale cinq, une erreur que je souhaite signaler.
common_error.explanation: It is common for Spanish speakers to use the symbol '2+2=5' in formal presentations, but in French it is preferable to write numbers in full letters for a formal register. Additionally, 'c'est' is used generally, but it is often overused; in formal French, more varied structures such as 'voici', 'il s'agit de' or 'cela représente' are preferred.

examples.original: Mesdames, Messieurs, bonjour à toutes et à tous.
examples.phonetic: /me dam, me sje, bɔ̃ʒuʁ a tut e a tu/
examples.translation: Señoras, señores, buenos días a todas y a todos.
examples.note: In formal French, the greeting is made with 'Mesdames, Messieurs' and 'à toutes et à tous' is included to be inclusive.

examples.original: Je tiens à remercier chaleureusement les organisateurs de cette manifestation.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə tjɛ̃ a ʁəmeʁsje ʃalœʁøzəmɑ̃ le zɔʁɡanizatœʁ də sɛt maniʃɛstɑ̃/
examples.translation: Quiero agradecer calurosamente a los organizadores de este evento.
examples.note: The structure 'je tiens à + infinitive' is typical of formal register to express a firm desire.

examples.original: Je suis honoré(e) de prendre la parole devant vous.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə sɥi zɔnɔʁe də pʁɑ̃dʁ la paʁɔl dəvɑ̃ vu/
examples.translation: Es un honor tomar la palabra ante ustedes.
examples.note: The participle 'honoré' agrees with the speaker's gender; in French, the '@' symbol is not used as in Spanish.

examples.original: Premièrement, je vais aborder la situation actuelle.
examples.phonetic: /pʁəmjɛʁmɑ̃, ʒə ve abɔʁde la sitɥasjɔ̃ aktyɛl/
examples.translation: En primer lugar, voy a abordar la situación actual.
examples.note: Adverbs such as 'premièrement', 'deuxièmement' and 'troisièmement' are used to structure the presentation clearly.

examples.original: Passons maintenant au deuxième point de mon exposé.
examples.phonetic: /pɛsɔ̃ mɛ̃tənɑ̃ o døzjɛm pwɛ̃ də mɔ̃n‿ekspoze/
examples.translation: Pasemos ahora al segundo punto de mi exposición.
examples.note: The imperative 'passons' with 'nous' is a way to engage the audience in the speech.

examples.original: En ce qui concerne ce dernier aspect, il convient de souligner que...
examples.phonetic: /ɑ̃ sə ki kɔ̃sɛʁn sə dɛʁnje aspɛ, il kɔ̃vjɛ də suliɲe kə/
examples.translation: En lo que respecta a este último aspecto, conviene subrayar que...
examples.note: The expression 'il convient de + infinitive' is neutral and formal for making a recommendation.

examples.original: En conclusion, je voudrais insister sur l'importance de ce projet.
examples.phonetic: /ɑ̃ kɔ̃klyzjɔ̃, ʒə vudʁe ɛ̃siste syʁ l‿ɛ̃pɔʁtɑ̃s də sə pʁɔʒɛ/
examples.translation: En conclusión, quisiera insistir en la importancia de este proyecto.
examples.note: The conditional 'voudrais' softens the desire, making the statement sound more polite and less imposing.

examples.original: En vous remerciant de votre attention, je vous laisse à votre réflexion.
examples.phonetic: /ɑ̃ vu ʁəmeʁsjɑ̃ də vɔtʁ atɑ̃sjɔ̃, ʒə vu lɛs a vɔtʁ ʁeflɛksjɔ̃/
examples.translation: Agradeciéndoles su atención, les dejo a su reflexión.
examples.note: The compound gerund 'en vous remerciant' is a formal construction to thank at the end.

examples.original: Je vous remercie de votre écoute et reste à votre disposition pour toute question.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə vu ʁəmeʁsi də vɔtʁ ekut e ʁɛst a vɔtʁ dispozisjɔ̃ puʁ tut kɛstjɔ̃/
examples.translation: Les agradezco su atención y quedo a su disposición para cualquier pregunta.
examples.note: 'Reste à votre disposition' is a fixed collocation used in formal contexts to offer further assistance.

title: Rédiger des textes académiques complexes / Academic writing
bridge: In academic French, nominalization and impersonal constructions are much more common than in Spanish. While Spanish tends to use personal verbs ('se observa que...'), French prefers abstract nouns ('l'observation de...') and the passive voice with 'il est' + participe passé. Be careful with connectors: 'en effet' is not 'en efecto' (which would be 'de hecho'), and 'd'ailleurs' does not always mean 'además'. Additionally, expressing cause and consequence requires nuances that in Spanish are resolved with a single connector.
rule: To write academic texts in French at C1 level, you must master: (1) Nominalization: turning verbs into nouns (analyser → l'analyse, observer → l'observation), which gives a more abstract and formal tone. (2) Impersonal constructions: 'il est + adjectif + de + infinitif' (il est essentiel de...), 'il convient de', 'il s'avère que', 'il ressort que'. (3) The passive voice with indefinite pronoun 'on' or impersonal 'il': 'on observe', 'il a été démontré'. (4) Logical connectors: cause ('en raison de', 'du fait que', 'étant donné que'), consequence ('par conséquent', 'de ce fait', 'en conséquence'), opposition ('néanmoins', 'toutefois', 'en revanche'), concession ('bien que + subjonctif', 'quoique'). (5) The subjunctive after impersonal expressions of opinion or necessity: 'il est nécessaire que + subjonctif'. Exception: with 'il est probable que' the indicative is used. (6) The use of 'dont' and 'lequel' for complex relative clauses. Pay attention to the agreement of the past participle with the auxiliary 'avoir' when the direct object precedes the verb (la thèse que j'ai rédigée).

concept_examples.text: L'analyse des données révèle une corrélation significative entre les variables.
concept_examples.translation: The analysis of the data reveals a significant correlation between the variables.
concept_examples.phonetic: /l‿a.naliz de done ʁə.vɛl yn kɔ.ʁe.la.sjɔ̃ si.ɲi.fi.ka.tiv ɑ̃tʁ le va.ʁjabl/

concept_examples.text: Il est essentiel de considérer les limites méthodologiques de cette étude.
concept_examples.translation: It is essential to consider the methodological limitations of this study.
concept_examples.phonetic: /il ɛ.t‿e.sɑ̃.sjɛl də kɔ̃.si.de.ʁe le li.mit me.tɔ.dɔ.lɔ.ʒik də sɛt‿e.tyd/

concept_examples.text: Bien que les résultats soient prometteurs, des recherches supplémentaires sont nécessaires.
concept_examples.translation: Although the results are promising, additional research is necessary.
concept_examples.phonetic: /bjɛ̃ kə le ʁe.zyl.ta swa pʁɔ.mɛ.tœʁ, de ʁə.ʃɛʁʃ sy.ple.mɑ̃.tɛʁ sɔ̃ ne.se.sɛʁ/

concept_examples.text: La thèse que j'ai rédigée porte sur l'impact des politiques éducatives.
concept_examples.translation: The thesis I wrote focuses on the impact of educational policies.
concept_examples.phonetic: /la tɛz kə ʒe ʁe.di.ʒe pɔʁt syʁ lɛ̃.pakt de pɔ.li.tik e.dy.ka.tiv/

common_error.wrong: En effet, les résultats sont différents de ce qu'on attendait.
common_error.correct: De fait, les résultats sont différents de ce qu'on attendait.
common_error.correct_alt: Effectivement, les résultats sont différents de ce qu'on attendait.
common_error.explanation: The error stems from the influence of the Spanish 'en efecto'. In French, 'en effet' means 'because' or 'indeed' in the sense of justification, not confirmation. To confirm something, 'de fait' or 'effectivement' is used. In academic contexts, 'en effet' introduces an explanation or cause, not a statement.

examples.original: La transformation du système éducatif a été étudiée.
examples.phonetic: /la tʁɑ̃s.fɔʁ.ma.sjɔ̃ dy sis.tɛm e.dy.ka.tif a e.te e.ty.dje/
examples.translation: The transformation of the educational system has been studied.
examples.note: Note that Spanish uses the passive form 'ha sido estudiada', while French prefers the passive with 'été' + past participle. The nominalization of the verb 'transformer' into 'transformation' is typical of academic register.

examples.original: L'évaluation des risques nécessite une approche prudente.
examples.phonetic: /le.va.lja.sjɔ̃ de ʁisk ne.se.sit yn a.pʁɔʃ pʁy.dɑ̃t/
examples.translation: The evaluation of risks requires a cautious approach.
examples.note: Observe that French uses 'des' (de + les) while Spanish uses 'de los'. Nominalization avoids the verbal construction 'évaluer les risques'.

examples.original: On observe une augmentation des dépenses publiques.
examples.phonetic: /ɔ̃ ɔb.sɛʁv yn og.mɑ̃.ta.sjɔ̃ de de.pɑ̃s py.blik/
examples.translation: An increase in public spending is observed.
examples.note: The impersonal 'on' in French is equivalent to the impersonal 'se' in Spanish. It is much more common than 'nous' in academic texts.

examples.original: Il convient de mentionner les limites de cette approche.
examples.phonetic: /il kɔ̃.vjɛ̃ də mɑ̃.sjɔ.ne le li.mit də sɛt a.pʁɔʃ/
examples.translation: It is advisable to mention the limitations of this approach.
examples.note: The construction 'il convient de + infinitif' is very formal. In Spanish we use 'conviene', but French requires the impersonal 'il'.

examples.original: Il a été démontré que la théorie est insuffisante.
examples.phonetic: /il a e.te de.mɔ̃.tʁe kə la te.ɔ.ʁi ɛ.t‿ɛ̃.sy.fi.zɑ̃t/
examples.translation: It has been demonstrated that the theory is insufficient.
examples.note: The impersonal passive with 'il a été démontré que' avoids mentioning the agent. In Spanish it is expressed as 'se ha demostrado'.

examples.original: Il s'avère que les résultats sont contradictoires.
examples.phonetic: /il sa.vɛʁ kə le ʁe.zyl.ta sɔ̃ kɔ̃.tʁa.dik.twaʁ/
examples.translation: It turns out that the results are contradictory.
examples.note: 'Il s'avère que' is an impersonal pronominal verb; its use indicates a discovery. Do not confuse with 's'avérer' (to turn out), which in Spanish does not require 'se'.

examples.original: Étant donné que les ressources sont limitées, il est prioritaire de réduire les coûts.
examples.phonetic: /e.tɑ̃ dɔ.ne kə le ʁə.suʁs sɔ̃ li.mi.te, il ɛ pʁi.jɔ.ʁi.tɛʁ də ʁe.dɥiʁ le ku/
examples.translation: Given that resources are limited, it is a priority to reduce costs.
examples.note: The connector 'étant donné que' is more formal than 'parce que'. In Spanish 'dado que' is used, but French requires the compound gerund.

examples.original: Les résultats sont significatifs ; en revanche, la taille de l'échantillon est insuffisante.
examples.phonetic: /le ʁe.zyl.ta sɔ̃ si.ɲi.fi.ka.tif ; ɑ̃ ʁə.vɑ̃ʃ, la taj də le.ʃɑ̃.ti.jɔ̃ ɛ.t‿ɛ̃.sɥi.fi.zɑ̃t/
examples.translation: The results are significant; however, the sample size is insufficient.
examples.note: 'En revanche' is used to oppose two ideas but with a nuance of compensation. Do not confuse with 'd'ailleurs' (on the other hand).

examples.original: Quoique l'étude soit limitée, elle apporte des éléments nouveaux.
examples.phonetic: /kwa.kə le.tyd swa li.mi.te, ɛl a.pɔʁt de.ze.le.mɑ̃ nu.vo/
examples.translation: Although the study may be limited, it brings new elements.
examples.note: After 'quoique' and 'bien que', the subjunctive is used. In Spanish 'aunque' can take the indicative or subjunctive depending on context, but in French it always requires the subjunctive.

title: Stratégies de négociation avancées / Advanced negotiation strategies
bridge: In French, advanced negotiation requires subtle handling of politeness and assertion. Unlike Spanish, where one can be direct with 'no' or 'I want', French tends to use circumlocutions and conditionals to soften opposition. Be careful with the 'si' of opposition: in French, 'si' answers affirmatively to a negative question, whereas in Spanish we also use 'sí' to contradict, but the structure differs. Additionally, the nuances of 'tu' and 'vous' are crucial: using 'vous' in formal negotiation creates professional distance, but an unexpected shift to 'tu' can be a strategic tool for rapprochement, something less common in Spanish.
rule: To express concession and counterproposal in French: use 'certes... mais', 'bien que + subjonctif', 'tout en + participe présent'. To politely reject: 'je ne pense pas que ce soit possible' (subjonctif), 'je crains que... ne' (ne explétif). To insist: 'je tiens à souligner que', 'il me semble essentiel de'. The conditional of politeness (je voudrais, j'aurais besoin) is essential. In negotiation, the 'futur antérieur' is often used for closed hypotheses: 'nous aurions pu'. Intonation and word order are key; French does not have Spanish-style double negation, but it does have complex negation: 'ne... point' (formal), 'ne... aucun'. Remember that 'si' is only used to contradict a negative question: 'Tu ne veux pas ? – Si, je veux.'

concept_examples.text: Je comprends votre position, cependant je ne peux pas accepter cette offre.
concept_examples.translation: I understand your position, however I cannot accept this offer.
concept_examples.phonetic: ʒə kɔ̃pʁɑ̃ vɔtʁ pɔzisjɔ̃, səpɑ̃dɑ̃ ʒə nə pə pa aksepte sɛt ɔfʁ

concept_examples.text: Si vous pouviez réduire le prix, nous serions prêts à conclure.
concept_examples.translation: If you could reduce the price, we would be ready to close.
concept_examples.phonetic: si vu puvi e ʁedɥiʁ lə pʁi, nu səʁjɔ̃ pʁɛ a kɔ̃klyʁ

concept_examples.text: Je crains que cette condition ne soit pas acceptable.
concept_examples.translation: I fear this condition may not be acceptable.
concept_examples.phonetic: ʒə kʁɛ̃ kə sɛt kɔ̃disjɔ̃ nə swa pa aksɛptabl

concept_examples.text: Nous pourrions peut-être envisager une solution alternative.
concept_examples.translation: We could perhaps consider an alternative solution.
concept_examples.phonetic: nu puʁjɔ̃ pøtɛtʁ ɑ̃vizaʒe yn sɔlysjɔ̃ altɛʁnativ

common_error.wrong: Je ne suis pas d'accord, je veux un autre prix.
common_error.correct: Je ne suis pas tout à fait d'accord, je préférerais discuter du prix.
common_error.correct_alt: Je ne peux pas me rallier à ce prix, pourrions-nous en reparler ?
common_error.explanation: The typical error of Spanish speakers is being too direct when saying 'je veux' (I want) or 'je ne suis pas d'accord' (I don't agree). In French, in negotiation contexts, the conditional ('je préférerais') and impersonal forms ('pourrions-nous') are preferred. Additionally, 'd'accord' can sound categorical; it is softened with 'tout à fait' or 'entièrement'. French politeness requires implicit justification: instead of 'quiero', one uses 'j'aurais besoin de' or 'il me faudrait'.

examples.original: Je vous accorde une remise de 5%.
examples.phonetic: ʒə vu zakɔʁd yn ʁəmiz də sɛ̃k puʁsɑ̃
examples.translation: I grant you a 5% discount.
examples.note: The verb 'accorder' is formal and used in official concessions.

examples.original: En contrepartie, j'aimerais un délai supplémentaire.
examples.phonetic: ɑ̃ kɔ̃tʁəpaʁi, ʒɛmʁɛ œ̃ delɛ sɥplemɑ̃tɛʁ
examples.translation: In return, I would like an additional deadline.
examples.note: 'En contrepartie' is equivalent to 'in return', but more negotiatory.

examples.original: C'est un compromis raisonnable, mais il me faut des garanties.
examples.phonetic: sɛ t‿ɛ̃ kɔ̃pʁɔmi ʁɛzɔnabl, mɛ il mə fo de ɡaʁɑ̃ti
examples.translation: It's a reasonable compromise, but I need guarantees.
examples.note: The structure 'il me faut' is more idiomatic than 'je dois avoir'.

examples.original: Je ne pense pas que ce soit la meilleure solution.
examples.phonetic: ʒə nə pɑ̃s pa kə sə swa la mɛjœʁ sɔlysjɔ̃
examples.translation: I don't think this is the best solution.
examples.note: The subjunctive 'soit' is mandatory after 'ne pas penser que'.

examples.original: Je crains que ce soit impossible à ce stade.
examples.phonetic: ʒə kʁɛ̃ kə sə swa ɛ̃pɔsibl a sə stad
examples.translation: I fear it may be impossible at this stage.
examples.note: The verb 'craindre' can take 'ne' explétif, but it is omitted here in informal register.

examples.original: Je suis au regret de vous informer que nous déclinons votre offre.
examples.phonetic: ʒə sɥi o ʁəɡʁɛ də vu z‿ɛ̃fɔʁme kə nu deklɛnɔ̃ vɔtʁ ɔfʁ
examples.translation: I regret to inform you that we are declining your offer.
examples.note: Extremely polite form; 'décliner' is more formal than 'refuser'.

examples.original: Et si nous envisagions un paiement échelonné ?
examples.phonetic: e si nu z‿ɑ̃vizaʒjɔ̃ œ̃ pɛmɑ̃ eʃlɔne
examples.translation: What if we considered an installment payment?
examples.note: 'Et si' + imperfect: very common hypothetical proposal in negotiation.

examples.original: Nous pourrions répartir les coûts différemment.
examples.phonetic: nu puʁjɔ̃ ʁepaʁtiʁ le ku difeʁamɑ̃
examples.translation: We could distribute the costs differently.
examples.note: The conditional 'pourrions' softens the proposal.

examples.original: Que diriez-vous d'un échange de services ?
examples.phonetic: kə diʁje vu d‿œ̃ eʃɑ̃ʒ də sɛʁvis
examples.translation: How about an exchange of services?
examples.note: 'Que diriez-vous de' is a polite formula for suggesting.

title: Nuancer son attitude / Expressing attitude and evaluation with nuances
bridge: In Spanish, we often use adverbs like 'francamente', 'honestamente' or 'por desgracia' to nuance an opinion. In French, in addition to adverbs, there are specific constructions such as 'il est + adjectif + de', the subjunctive after verbs of negated opinion, and the attenuating conditional (je dirais que, ce serait). A typical trap is to translate 'es una pena que' literally as 'c'est dommage que' + indicative, when French requires the subjunctive: 'c'est dommage qu'il soit parti'. Another key difference: French uses 'en' or 'y' in phrases like 'il en va de même', which have no direct equivalent in Spanish.
rule: To nuance attitude in French at C1 level, the following are used: 1) Modal adverbs: 'franchement', 'honnêtement', 'visiblement', 'manifestement', 'malheureusement', 'heureusement'. 2) Impersonal constructions with subjunctive: 'il est + adjectif + que + subjonctif' (e.g., il est regrettable qu'il parte). 3) The attenuating conditional: 'je dirais', 'je pourrais', 'ce serait', to soften statements. 4) The subjunctive after negated opinion or doubt verbs: 'je ne pense pas qu'il vienne', 'je doute qu'il réussisse'. 5) Idiomatic expressions: 'il n'en reste pas moins que', 'force est de constater que', 'il s'en faut de peu que'. Note: not all adjectives require the subjunctive; some with certainty use the indicative (il est certain que). Formal register requires the subjunctive after 'il semble que' (though informally the indicative is sometimes used).

concept_examples.text: Franchement, je pense que cette décision est discutable.
concept_examples.translation: Frankly, I think this decision is debatable.
concept_examples.phonetic: fʁɑ̃ʃ.mɑ̃ ʒə pɑ̃s kə sɛt de.si.zjɔ̃ ɛ dis.ky.tabl

concept_examples.text: Il est regrettable que vous n'ayez pas assisté à la réunion.
concept_examples.translation: It's regrettable that you didn't attend the meeting.
concept_examples.phonetic: il ɛ ʁə.ɡʁɛ.tabl kə vu n‿ɛ.je pa a.sis.te a la ʁe.y.njɔ̃

concept_examples.text: Je dirais que ce projet manque un peu d'ambition.
concept_examples.translation: I would say this project lacks a bit of ambition.
concept_examples.phonetic: ʒə di.ʁɛ kə sə pʁɔ.ʒɛ mɑ̃k œ̃ pø d‿ɑ̃.bi.sjɔ̃

concept_examples.text: Force est de constater que les résultats sont décevants.
concept_examples.translation: It must be acknowledged that the results are disappointing.
concept_examples.phonetic: fɔʁs ɛ də kɔ̃s.ta.te ke le ʁe.zyl.ta sɔ̃ de.sə.vɑ̃

common_error.correct_alt: Il est dommage qu'il soit parti.
common_error.explanation: The error comes from the literal translation of the Spanish 'es una pena que ha ido' (indicative). In French, after 'c'est dommage que', 'il est dommage que' and other impersonal expressions of feeling, the subjunctive is required. The indicative ('est') is incorrect. Remember: after expressions of emotion or evaluation, use the subjunctive.

examples.original: Franchement, ce n'est pas terrible.
examples.phonetic: fʁɑ̃ʃ.mɑ̃ sə n‿ɛ pa tɛ.ʁibl
examples.translation: Frankly, it's not great.
examples.note: 'Franchement' is placed at the beginning or after the verb, and is used to introduce a sincere opinion.

examples.original: Visiblement, il n'a pas compris la question.
examples.phonetic: vi.zi.blə.mɑ̃ il n‿a pa kɔ̃.pʁi la kɛs.tjɔ̃
examples.translation: Clearly, he didn't understand the question.
examples.note: 'Visiblement' indicates an evaluation based on evidence, similar to 'por lo visto'.

examples.original: Malheureusement, l'offre a été retirée.
examples.phonetic: ma.lœ.ʁøz.mɑ̃ l‿ɔfʁ a e.te ʁə.ti.ʁe
examples.translation: Unfortunately, the offer was withdrawn.
examples.note: 'Malheureusement' expresses regret; it's more formal than 'dommage'.

examples.original: Il est important que tu sois présent demain.
examples.phonetic: il ɛ ɛ̃.pɔʁ.tɑ̃ kə ty swa pʁe.zɑ̃ də.mɛ̃
examples.translation: It's important that you be present tomorrow.
examples.note: After 'il est important que', the subjunctive (sois) is used, not the indicative.

examples.original: Je ne pense pas qu'il vienne ce soir.
examples.phonetic: ʒə nə pɑ̃s pa k‿il vjɛn sə swaʁ
examples.translation: I don't think he's coming tonight.
examples.note: The negation of an opinion verb ('penser') requires the subjunctive in the subordinate clause.

examples.original: Il semble que les négociations aient échoué.
examples.phonetic: il sɑ̃bl kə le ne.ɡɔ.sja.sjɔ̃ ɛ e.ʃwe
examples.translation: It seems the negotiations have failed.
examples.note: Although the indicative is sometimes used in informal register, the correct usage after 'il semble que' is the subjunctive (aient).

examples.original: Je dirais que ce film mérite le détour.
examples.phonetic: ʒə di.ʁɛ kə sə film me.ʁit lə de.tuʁ
examples.translation: I would say this film is worth watching.
examples.note: The conditional 'dirais' softens the statement, giving it a more humble tone.

examples.original: Il n'en reste pas moins que le problème est urgent.
examples.phonetic: il n‿ɑ̃ ʁɛst pa mwɛ̃ kə lə pʁɔ.blɛm ɛ yʁ.ʒɑ̃
examples.translation: It doesn't change the fact that the problem is urgent.
examples.note: This idiomatic expression introduces a concessive nuance, similar to 'no obstante'.

examples.original: Ce serait une erreur de sous-estimer ses capacités.
examples.phonetic: sə sə.ʁɛ yn ɛ.ʁœʁ də su.z‿ɛs.ti.me se ka.pa.si.te
examples.translation: It would be a mistake to underestimate his abilities.
examples.note: The conditional 'serait' attenuates the statement and makes it less categorical.

translations.en: Expressing attitude and evaluation with nuances

title: Changement de registre / Change of register
bridge: In Spanish, register change (formal, neutral, familiar) is marked by the choice of tú/usted, but in French the system is richer: there are three registers (soutenu, courant, familier) and the use of 'vous' for politeness is more frequent than in Spain. Additionally, colloquial spoken French uses negation without 'ne' and structures like 'on' instead of 'nous', which would sound too informal in Spanish if translated literally. Be careful with false friends: 'sympa' is not always 'simpático' in all contexts, and 'bouquin' is only used in familiar register.
rule: In French, register is distinguished by: 1) Vocabulary (e.g., 'voiture' (courant) vs. 'bagnole' (familier), 'un livre' vs. 'un bouquin'); 2) Syntax (in soutenu style, the complete negation 'ne...pas' is used, in familier register 'ne' is omitted and 'on' is used instead of 'nous'); 3) Pronouns of address ('tu' vs. 'vous' depending on the situation and relationship); 4) Idiomatic expressions (e.g., 'avoir du bol' in familier vs. 'avoir de la chance' in courant). For C1 level, you must master register change according to social context: with friends, at work, in formal written texts. Avoid mixing levels: do not use 'truc' in a professional email, nor 'cependant' in a conversation between friends.

concept_examples.text: Soutenu : Je vous saurais gré de bien vouloir prendre en considération ma demande.
concept_examples.translation: I would be grateful if you would kindly consider my request.
concept_examples.phonetic: ʒə vu sɔʁɛ gʁe də bjɛ̃ vulwaʁ pʁɑ̃dʁ ɑ̃ kɔ̃sidɛʁasjɔ̃ ma dəmand

concept_examples.text: Courant : Pouvez-vous prendre ma demande en considération ?
concept_examples.translation: Can you consider my request?
concept_examples.phonetic: puve vu pʁɑ̃dʁ ma dəmɑ̃d ɑ̃ kɔ̃sidɛʁasjɔ̃

concept_examples.text: Familier : Tu peux jeter un œil à ma demande ?
concept_examples.translation: Can you take a look at my request?
concept_examples.phonetic: ty pø ʒəte œ̃ œj a ma dəmɑ̃d

concept_examples.text: Familier (oral) : T'as vu la meuf ? Elle est trop sympa.
concept_examples.translation: Have you seen the chick? She's really nice.
concept_examples.phonetic: ta vy la mœf ɛl ɛ tʁo sɛ̃pa

common_error.wrong: Je suis désolé, mais je ne peux pas venir à la réunion. J'ai un truc important à faire.
common_error.correct: Je suis désolé, mais je ne peux pas assister à la réunion. J'ai une obligation importante.
common_error.correct_alt: Je suis navré, mais je ne pourrai pas me rendre à la réunion. Un engagement urgent m'en empêche.
common_error.explanation: In a formal email, the use of 'truc' (familiar) is a register error. In Spanish, 'truco' or 'cosa' may work in informal contexts, but in formal French you must choose more precise vocabulary. Use 'obligation', 'engagement' or 'rendez-vous' in courant or soutenu register.

examples.original: Je vous serais reconnaissant de bien vouloir répondre à ma lettre dans les plus brefs délais.
examples.phonetic: ʒə vu səʁɛ ʁəkɔnɛsɑ̃ də bjɛ̃ vulwaʁ ʁepɔ̃dʁ a ma lɛtʁ dɑ̃ le ply bʁɛf dəlɛ
examples.translation: I would be grateful if you would kindly respond to my letter as soon as possible.
examples.note: Use of conditional for politeness and 'bien vouloir' to express a formal request.

examples.original: Veuillez agréer, Monsieur, l'expression de mes salutations distinguées.
examples.phonetic: vœje aɡʁee məsjø lɛkspʁɛsjɔ̃ də me salytasjɔ̃ dɛstɛ̃ɡe
examples.translation: Please accept, sir, the expression of my most distinguished regards.
examples.note: Typical closing formula in formal letters. 'Veuillez' is the imperative of 'vouloir' with a pleading tone.

examples.original: Il est impératif que vous fournissiez ces documents avant lundi.
examples.phonetic: il ɛt‿ɛ̃peʁatif kə vu fuʁnisje se dɔkymɑ̃ avɑ̃ lɛ̃di
examples.translation: It is imperative that you provide these documents before Monday.
examples.note: The subjunctive after 'impératif que' marks formality, similar to the use of the subjunctive in Spanish.

examples.original: Pouvez-vous m'envoyer le rapport pour demain ?
examples.phonetic: puve vu mɑ̃vwaʁ lə ʁapɔʁ puʁ dəmɛ̃
examples.translation: Can you send me the report for tomorrow?
examples.note: Use of 'pouvez-vous' with inversion, typical of the courant register. Not as formal as 'auriez-vous l'obligeance'.

examples.original: Je suis désolée, mais je ne pourrai pas venir à la fête.
examples.phonetic: ʒə sɥi dezɔle mɛ ʒə nə puʁe pa vniʁ a la fɛt
examples.translation: I'm sorry, but I won't be able to come to the party.
examples.note: Negation with 'ne...pas' is mandatory in written register, but in informal conversation it is often omitted.

examples.original: On a décidé de changer le projet, si tu es d'accord.
examples.phonetic: ɔ̃ a deside də ʃɑ̃ʒe lə pʁɔʒɛ si ty ɛ daˈkɔʁ
examples.translation: We've decided to change the project, if you agree.
examples.note: Although 'on' is grammatically singular, in courant register it replaces 'nous'. In Spanish 'cambiamos' is used, but the structure is different here.

examples.original: T'as vu la meuf qui vient de s'asseoir ?
examples.phonetic: ta vy la mœf ki vjɛ̃ də saswaʁ
examples.translation: Have you seen the chick who just sat down?
examples.note: 'Meuf' is apocope of 'femme' in verlan. Omitting 'ne' in 'tu as' -> 't'as' is very common in spoken register.

examples.original: Il a déchiré son ex en deux secondes pendant le dîner.
examples.phonetic: il a deʃiʁe sɔ̃ ɛks ɑ̃ dø səɡɔ̃d pɑ̃dɑ̃ lə dine
examples.translation: He tore his ex apart in two seconds during dinner.
examples.note: The expression 'déchirer' (literally 'to tear') is a metaphor in informal speech for harshly criticizing. In Spanish it would be 'destrozar', but with a colloquial nuance.

examples.original: On s'est fait jeter du bar hier soir, trop nuls les videurs.
examples.phonetic: ɔ̃ sɛ fɛ ʒəte dy baʁ iʁ swaʁ tʁo nyl le vidœʁ
examples.translation: They kicked us out of the bar last night, the bouncers are useless.
examples.note: Very informal register: use of 'on' for 'nous', omission of 'ne' in 's'est fait' (actually there is no 'ne' because it's affirmative, but 'trop nuls' is used instead of 'très nuls' for colloquial emphasis).

title: La communication interculturelle : nuances pragmatiques / Intercultural communication: pragmatic nuances
bridge: In French, politeness and social distance are marked much more through syntax and vocabulary than in Spanish. While in Spanish we use the conditional for politeness ('me gustaría') and the subjunctive to soften requests, in French impersonal structures ('il faudrait'), the polite imperfect ('je voulais vous demander') and a range of connectors and ritualized formulas are used depending on the register. Additionally, the use of 'tu' and 'vous' is stricter than the informal 'tuteo' in Spanish; a typical error is using 'tu' with strangers or in formal contexts, which is perceived as impolite or intrusive. French speakers also avoid direct 'no' in social situations, preferring circumlocutions like 'je ne sais pas' or 'on verra', whereas in Spanish we are more direct when rejecting.
rule: To manage intercultural communication in French at C1 level, you must master: (1) The tú/vous opposition: 'vous' is mandatory with strangers, older people, superiors and in professional contexts; 'tu' requires reciprocity and trust. The switch from 'vous' to 'tu' must be explicitly proposed (e.g. 'Je peux te tutoyer ?'). (2) The conditional for politeness: 'Je voudrais', 'J'aimerais' for requests; but the polite imperfect is also used in formulas like 'Je voulais vous demander' (more attenuated). (3) Softening strategies: 'un peu', 'peut-être', 'je pense que', 'je crois que' soften statements. (4) The subjunctive after negative opinion or necessity expressions: 'Il faut que vous sachiez'. (5) Ritualized formulas: to interrupt ('Pardon, puis-je me permettre ?'), to refuse ('Je suis désolé, mais...'), to thank ('Je vous suis très reconnaissant'), to say goodbye in formal contexts ('Je vous prie d'agréer, Monsieur/Madame, l'expression de mes salutations distinguées'). To avoid misunderstandings, adapt your register to the channel (written vs. oral) and the degree of formality. In French, negative politeness (avoiding imposition) is more prevalent than in Spanish; hence, indirect requests and questions with 'est-ce que' or inversion are common. Do not forget discourse markers that show nuanced agreement or disagreement: 'en effet', 'effectivement', 'certes, mais', 'il est vrai que', etc.

concept_examples.text: Je voudrais vous demander un conseil, si vous le permettez.
concept_examples.translation: I would like to ask you for advice, if you permit me.
concept_examples.phonetic: ʒə vudʁe vu dəmɑ̃dʁ ɛ̃ kɔ̃sɛj si vu lə pɛʁmɛt

concept_examples.text: Il faudrait peut-être en parler au directeur avant de prendre une décision.
concept_examples.translation: Perhaps we should talk to the director before making a decision.
concept_examples.phonetic: il fodʁɛ pətɛt ɑ̃ paʁle o diʁɛktœʁ ɑ̃ də pʁɑ̃dʁ yn desizjɔ̃

concept_examples.text: Je suis vraiment désolé, mais il m'est impossible de vous aider dans cette affaire.
concept_examples.translation: I am truly sorry, but it is impossible for me to help you with this matter.
concept_examples.phonetic: ʒə sɥi vʁɛmɑ̃ dezɔle mɛ il mɛt ɛ̃pɔsib də vu ɛde dɑ̃ sɛt afɛʁ

concept_examples.text: Pourriez-vous me dire où se trouve la gare, s'il vous plaît ?
concept_examples.translation: Could you tell me where the train station is, please?
concept_examples.phonetic: puʁje vu mə diʁ u sə tʁuv la ɡaʁ sil vu plɛ

common_error.wrong: Je te demande si tu peux m'aider (dicho a un desconocido).
common_error.correct: Je vous demande si vous pourriez m'aider.
common_error.explanation: The error consists of using 'te' (informal 'you') with a stranger, which in French is considered a violation of politeness norms. In Spanish, informal 'tuteo' is more widespread, but in French 'vous' is used with strangers and in formal situations until a relationship of trust is established. To avoid this error, remember that 'vous' is the unmarked form; 'tu' is only used among friends, family, or when someone explicitly proposes it.

examples.original: Vous pouvez me tutoyer, si vous voulez.
examples.phonetic: vu puve mə tytwaje si vu vule
examples.translation: You can use 'tu' with me, if you like.
examples.note: The offer to use informal 'tu' is usually phrased with 'tutoyer' + condition. The use of 'vous' is mandatory until the informal 'tu' is proposed.

examples.original: Je vous remercie pour votre aide.
examples.phonetic: ʒə vu ʁəmɛʁsi puʁ vɔtʁ ɛd
examples.translation: I thank you for your help.
examples.note: In formal contexts, 'vous' is used even in expressions of thanks. Avoid a simple 'merci' in very formal situations; add 'je vous remercie' for greater politeness.

examples.original: Tu peux passer me voir quand tu veux.
examples.phonetic: ty pə pase mə vwaʁ kɑ̃ ty vø
examples.translation: You can come by to see me whenever you want.
examples.note: In relationships of trust, 'tu' is used without issues, but you must know when it is appropriate (friends, close colleagues).

examples.original: Je ne suis pas tout à fait d'accord avec vous.
examples.phonetic: ʒə nə sɥi pa tut a fɛ dakɔʁ avɛk vu
examples.translation: I am not entirely in agreement with you.
examples.note: The softener 'pas tout à fait' softens disagreement instead of a direct 'No I don't agree'.

examples.original: Je crois que ce serait peut-être mieux de reporter la réunion.
examples.phonetic: ʒə kʁwa kə sə səʁɛ pətɛt mjø də ʁəpɔʁte la ʁeɥɲɔ̃
examples.translation: I think perhaps it would be better to postpone the meeting.
examples.note: The conditional 'serait' + 'peut-être' + 'je crois' deliberately shows uncertainty to avoid imposing.

examples.original: Il est possible que nous ayons un problème avec le calendrier.
examples.phonetic: il ɛ pɔsibl kə nu ɛjɔ̃ ɛ̃ pʁɔblɛm avɛk lə kalɑ̃dʁije
examples.translation: It is possible that we may have a problem with the schedule.
examples.note: The subjunctive after 'il est possible que' expresses uncertainty in a polite manner.

examples.original: Je vous prie d'agréer, Madame, l'expression de mes salutations distinguées.
examples.phonetic: ʒə vu pʁi daɡʁee madam lɛkspʁɛsjɔ̃ də me salytasjɔ̃ distɛ̃ɡe
examples.translation: I kindly ask you, Madam, to accept the expression of my distinguished greetings.
examples.note: Closing formula in formal letters. Variant with Monsieur: 'Je vous prie d'agréer, Monsieur, mes salutations distinguées'.

examples.original: Pourrais-je me permettre une remarque ?
examples.phonetic: puʁɛʒ mə pɛʁmɛtʁ yn ʁəmaʁk
examples.translation: May I be permitted to make a remark?
examples.note: This formula questions and softens the intrusion; useful in meetings or formal contexts.

examples.original: Je serais heureux de vous rencontrer pour en discuter plus en détail.
examples.phonetic: ʒə səʁɛz œʁø də vu ʁɑ̃kɔ̃te puʁ ɑ̃ diskyte plyz ɑ̃ detaj
examples.translation: I would be happy to meet you to discuss it in more detail.
examples.note: The conditional 'serais' expresses polite desire, typical of professional correspondence.

examples.original: Cela dit, je pense que nous devrions considérer une autre option.
examples.phonetic: səla di ʒə pɑ̃s kə nu dəvʁjɔ̃ kɔ̃sideʁe yn ɔtʁ ɔpsjɔ̃
examples.translation: That said, I think we should consider another option.
examples.note: The discourse marker 'cela dit' introduces a soft objection, very useful in discussions.
